Opinion of the Judge : Charges not proved J UD GM E N T The ACP, Yeshwanthapura Sub-division, Bengaluru has submitted Charge-sheet against the accused for the offences punishable under Section U/sec.498A, 304(B) of IPC & u/s.3(2)(v) of the SC/ST (POA) Act, 2015.

2. The brief facts of the prosecution case is that, she married accused falling in love and expressed his desire to marry the complainant, as such on 1.7.2018 in Gayathri temple, Yeshwanthapura, by receiving golden dollar as dowry accused married the victim in presence of his parents and daughter of complainant Smt.K.Uma.

The complainant submits the victim Rashmi was working in SAPL Garments in TVS Cross and accused was also working in the same garments, they fell in love and accused expressed his desire to marry the victim.
It has been informed to the accused that the complainant and victim were belonging to Adi Karnataka caste and only when they are convinced that he will look after well then only they will give.

After this as the victim had fallen in love with one Virupaksha and she became pregnant, later the said Virupaksha refused to marry her, as such crime was registered and there is a daughter born out of the wedlock aged about 6 months.
The accused accepted all these facts and even then he insisted to marry.
The marriage was performed on 1.7.2018.
The complainant submits after marriage the victim and the accused started residing in Doddabidarakallu, after marriage for about 6 months accused took care of the victim very well.

After this, accused had taken the hangings of the victim and necklace and golden chain and pledged them before Sait and obtained money, in fact though accused promised to get the same released, he failed,
the daughter of the complainant was so much distressed due to the behaviour of the accused.
In fact accused once again insisted the victim to get partitioned the landed property of the complainant family situated at near Malavalli as he intends to take a site.
On this pretext accused asked the victim in all position, the manner being very much disturbed and distressed the victim committed suicide in the house of the accused at Doddabidarakallu.

Meantime before the victim hanged herself accused had quarreled with the victim for not bringing dowry, did abused the victim as ",
,   ,  ,   ,            
             " and even threatened the victim that he will kill her by throttling.
This fact has been informed by the victim over phone to the complainant.
In fact the complainant had talked over phone with the accused and directed not to give ill-treatment to the victim.
Even then accused used to give harassment, torture to the victim.
On the date of incident, accused had gone away, victim alone was in the house.

In fact the owner of the house also informed the victim that they should not quarrel with each other, otherwise they have to vacate the premises, being distressed by this accused harassment of the accused, on 10.6.2019 shifted to the house of Jagadish, 2nd floor, Maranna Layout and she cannot live alone in Bengaluru,
as such she informed she will not be residing there, on 16.6.2019 the victim had taken drum to have filled up with water in her matrimonial house, which have taken the house from the complainant, on 19.6.2019 when the complainant went to the house of the victim she informed they have gone to Mahadeshwara Betta and it is also informed while doing cooking the oil spilled over the leg of the victim, therefore she was alone in the house, after 4 days as victim never called the complainant, on 30.6.2019 at about 3.00 p.m the Peenya police called the complainant and informed the victim had bolted from inside, did not opened the house and she had hanged herself with saree and she had Peenya Ps vs H Suresh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108804952/
2 died, immediately complainant rushed to the Sapthagiri hospital where she found victim had died.
Accordingly having suspicion over the accused, reported the same before the Investigating Officer.

3. The Investigating officer after conclusion of investigation, on drawing of spot mahazar, has recorded the statement of witnesses and after collecting caste report of accused as well as of the CW-1, has filed charge sheet against the accused.
4.
During the course of investigation, the accused obtained bail.
After filing of charge sheet, this court took the cognizance of said offence and issued summons to the accused.
On service of the same, the accused has appeared before this Court and got enlarged on bail.
5. The charge sheet copies were furnished to the accused as contemplated under Section 207 of Cr.P.C. Heard before the charge.

As there was sufficient materials available, charge was framed for the offences punishable u/sec.498A, 304(B) of IPC & u/s.3(2)(v) of the SC/ST (POA) Act, 2015 read over and explained to the accused in vernacular language and he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
6. At trial the prosecution to establish the guilt of the accused got examined P.W.1 to P.W.8 and placed Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and M.Os.1 to 10.

The statement of the accused u/sec 313 recorded, read over and explained to the accused in vernacular language and the accused, denied all the incriminating evidence and he did not choose to lead defence evidence on his behalf.

2)Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused alongwith his parents gave mental and physical cruelty to the victim to bring more dowry and abused her in filthy language, due to which victim on 30.6.2019 at 3.00 p.m committed suicide by hanging to the ceiling fan and died and thereby committed the offence Punishable under Section 304(B) of IPC?

Peenya Ps vs H Suresh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108804952/
3 3) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on aforesaid date, time and place, the accused not being the members of SC/ST has committed murder of the deceased victim,
who belongs to scheduled caste and thereby je committed offence which is punishable with 10 years or imprisonment for life and thereby committed offences punishable under section 3(2)(v) of the SC and ST(Prevention of Atrocities) Act,?
4)What order?
8.

In the complaint, complainant specifically mentioned that accused and victim were residing in Doddabidarakallu wherein accused looked her for 6 months and after that he took of the golden ornaments given to the victim, namely only necklace, golden chain and one hangings which were pledged.
The amount was obtained by the accused.
In fact once again accused demanded dowry by directing the victim to bring amount to purchase the site in Bengaluru by selling the lands situated at Malavalli, the native of the father of the victim.
As such on 10.6.2019 he intimidated the victim assaulted and abused her by taking the caste name even threatened he will throttle the victim to death.
Being disturbed by the ill-treatment victim has committed suicide on 30.6.2019 is the allegation made in the complaint.
In fact the prosecution has placed the appraisal report and also the golden ornaments which were seized from the Pawn Broker which have been deposited in the P.R.No.414/2021 in this court.

The complainant in her evidence has deposed about giving of the golden ornaments, however she does not deposed in consonance with the complaint that accused had demanded dowry as mentioned in the complaint.
In the case on hand, P.W.1 has turned hostile.
The learned SPP has cross- examined her even then she does not support the prosecution with regard to demand of dowry.
In page- 6 of her cross-examination, she specifically denies only due to dowry demand her daughter committed suicide.

In the evidence of P.W.2 the brother of the victim deposed by turning hostile with regard to the demand of dowry even learned SPP crossed this witness in page-3 of his cross-examination, he does not know whether accused obtained golden ornaments at the time of giving his sister in marriage to accused.

This witness in page-3 specifically admits accused is to be given portion of the site and even accused used to abuse his sister and even she has been threatened being killed and this witness in cross-examination admits that his sister for that reason only committed suicide.
This witness has not been preferred to be cross-examined by the learned counsel for the accused.

In fact P.W.3 Madaiah has turned hostile to the case of prosecution,
even after cross-examining this witness with regard to abusing and demanding land by the accused is specifically denied.
This witness in page-4 specifically denied dowry demand is made by the accused.

The appraiser who had summoned and examined has identified the golden ornaments Peenya Ps vs H Suresh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108804952/
4 shown to him being worth as per his appraising made in court which is deposited in the court.
Another witness the P.W.4 Vishwanath has turned hostile.
Similarly the P.W.5 Shivashankar has also turned hostile, the P.W.6 Mahesh.K.N. has completely turned hostile, even after cross-examining nothing has been elicited so as to incriminate the accused.
The Investigating Officer has deposed about registering crime.

On the basis of the material on record, though the P.W.2 has admitted in his cross- examination made by the prosecution that only due to dowry demand made by the accused, victim had committed suicide.
However in the evidence of PWs.1 and 3 who are the parents of the victim have turned hostile.
Under such circumstances the ill-treatment made out by the accused and harassment made does not corroborates in the evidence of prosecution though P.W.2 supports the prosecution.

Under such circumstances the evidence of P.W.2 admitting about ill-treatment and harassment as per sec.498A cannot be presumed being committed by the accused in the absence of evidence of his own family members.
10. On going through the documents on record, as there are specific contradictions with regard to the demand of dowry, this court is satisfied to answer Point No.1 in the Negative.
11. POINT NO.2:

In proof of ingredients of alleged offence in the complaint, it has been specifically mentioned by the complainant and informed her daughter has committed suicide and she gave complaint against the accused being her son-in-law.

In support of the same in her examination-in-chief, she has turned hostile, even after cross-examining though admits the Ex.P.1,
but the contents have been disputed.
The P.W.2 Dileep.M also has turned hostile with regard to the victim had succumbed due to the accused giving harassment to her.
However in the cross-examination by learned SPP he supports the prosecution.
The P.W.3 Madaiah father of the victim does not support the prosecution case and even after cross-examining nothing has been elicited so as to incriminate the accused.

The P.W.6 Mahesh.K.N. friend of father of the victim deposed about death of victim, he had gone for inquest but this witness does not supports prosecution case with regard to death caused by the accused that only by the harassment given by the accused, by demanding the site and abusing the victim in filthy language.

Accordingly this court is satisfied in the absence of corroboration though the death of the victim is proved by the prosecution by examining P.W.7 who has deposed about conducting the P.M.Report, the Investigating Officer registering crime has been examined who deposed about the incident.

However based on the hostility of the complainant and her husband in the absence of corroboration with the allegations, this court is satisfied that the ingredients of offence punishable u/s.304(B) has not been established though the death of the victim is proved.
Under such circumstances this court is satisfied to answer Point No.2 in the Negative.
12. POINT NO.3:
On going through the materials on record, in the case on hand first offence is punishable u/sec.304(B) is punishable with imprisonment for less than 7 years.
As such, the charge punishable under section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (POA) Act, 1989 was framed.
In the case on hand, as offence punishable u/sec.304(B) of IPC being not established, yhe charge u/sec.3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act, 1989 does not survive to be independently proved.
Accordingly, point No.3 is answered in the Negative.

Peenya Ps vs H Suresh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108804952/
5 23.
POINT No.4 :- The accused did complied the provisions of section 437A of Cr.P.C., by providing personal bond before this court, for his appearance before the Hon'ble Appellant court.
On going through the material on record, the golden ornaments of the victim are being seized by the Investigating Officer and deposited in court.
After disposal of this case the same is to be returned to the complainant as interim custody and the same order shall be absolute after appeal period being over.

In view of my foregoing reasons, I proceed the pass the following;
OR D E R Acting under Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C, the accused is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 304(B) of IPC & u/s.3(2)(v) of the SC/ST (POA) Act, 2015.
The accused is set at liberty.
The Bail bond and surety bond furnished u/sec. 437A of Cr.P.C. will be in force for a period of 6 months from today in view of sec 437A of Cr.PC
After disposal of this case the golden ornaments shall be returned to the complainant as interim custody and the same order shall be absolute after appeal period being over.
(Dictated to the stenographer Grade I in open court, transcription thereof corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in open Court on this the 15 th day of March, 2024).
(Rajesh Karnam K) LXX Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge & Special Judge, Bangalore.
